en: O best of kings, your duty is to chastise those who act cruelly, who are engaged in sinful practices and who are devoid of the precepts of religion (Dharma, Artha and Kama.)

sa: तस्योपदेशं वक्ष्यामि यथावत् तन्निवोध मे। यैरैश्चारयन्नित्यं पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि॥
en: I shall communicate the instructions about it duly. Do you learn from me those doors by which directing the soul within the body one sees that which is without beginning and end.

sa: ध्यानयोगादुपागम्य निर्ममा निरहंकृताः। अव्यक्तं प्रविशन्तीह महतां लोकमुत्तमम्॥
en: Those persons who are freed from egoism and who are re-born after having attained to the fullness of Yoga contemplation, enter into the highest region reserved for the great, viz., the Unmanifest.

sa: सर्वागमानामाचारः प्रथमं परिकल्प्यते। आचारप्रभवो धर्मो धर्मस्य प्रभुरच्युतः॥
en: Conduct is said to be the foremost of all subjects treated of in the scriptures. Virtue has conduct for its root. The unfading Vasudeva is said to be the Lord of Virtue.

sa: रथैः सनन्दिघोषैश्च पृष्ठतः सोऽनुगम्यते॥ देवकन्याधिरूढस्तु भ्राजमानैः स्वलंकृतैः।
en: While making his journeys on his car, he is always followed by a large train of cars producing the most agreeable rattle and ridden by celestial ladies shining with ornaments and beauty.

sa: पितृन्णात् तारयति पुत्र इत्यनुशुश्रुमा पुत्रपौत्रेश्च नियतं साधुलोकानुपाश्नुते॥
en: The son is called Putra because he frees his ancestor's debt. Through sons and grandsons one always enjoys the happiness of those regions which are reserved for the pious and the good.

sa: इति पञ्चविधं दानं पुण्यकीर्तिविवर्धनम्। यथाशक्त्या प्रदातव्यमेवमाह प्रजापतिः॥
en: These are the five sorts of gift. They increase the giver's merits and fame. The Lord of all creatures has said that one should always make gifts according to his power. a

sa: प्रथमो ह्येष देवानां मुखादग्निमजीजनत्। ग्रहैर्बहुविधैः प्राणान् संरुद्धानुत्सृजत्यपि॥
en: He is the first of all the celestials, and it was from his mouth that he created Agni. That great deity, ever willing to grant protection to all, never forsakes his suppliants.

sa: अमृतेनावसिक्तश्च वृषदर्भो नरेश्वरः। दिव्यैश्च सुसुखैर्माल्यैरभिवृष्टः पुनः पुनः॥
en: King Vrishadarbha was bathed in a shower of nectar that was poured upon him. Garlands of celestials flowers, of sweet fragrance and touch, were also showered upon him copiously again and again.

sa: वैदेहकाच्च पापिष्ठा क्रूरं मायोपजीविनम्। निषादान्मद्रनाभं च खरयानप्रयायिनम्॥
en: From the Vaideha originates cruel and sinful caste that lives by practising deception. From the Nishadas again originates the Madranabha caste whose members are seen to ride on cars drawn by asses.

sa: आसमाप्तेश्च यज्ञस्य तस्यामितपराक्रमः॥ निकामवर्षी पर्जन्यो बभूव जनमेजय।
en: Indeed, O Janamejaya, till the completion of the sacrifice of the Rishi of great prowess, the deity of rain poured rain which met the wishes of men both about quantity and time.

sa: सर्वदानैर्गुरुतरं सर्वदानैर्विशिष्यते। पानीयं नरशार्दूल तस्माद् दातव्यमेव हि॥
en: The gift of drink, O chief of men, is superior to every other gift. In point of merit, it is superior to all other gifts. Therefore, do you make gifts of water.

sa: येऽपि संकीर्णकर्माणो राजानो रौद्रकर्मिणः। तेभ्यः पवित्रमाख्येयं भूमिदानमनुत्तमम्॥
en: Those kings who are mean in their acts or are of fierce deeds, should be taught that gift of earth is highly purifying and is at the same time the highest gift.

sa: प्रयास्यमानो नृपतिस्त्रिविधां परिचिन्तयेत्। आत्मनश्चैव शत्रोश्च शक्तिं शास्त्रविशारदः॥
en: The king, conversant with the scriptures, who marches against an enemy should think of the three kinds of strength, and, indeed, reflect on his own strength and the strength of his enemy.

sa: अनार्यत्वमनाचारः क्रूरत्वं निष्क्रियात्मता। पुरुषं व्यञ्जयन्तीह लोके कलुषयोनिजम्॥
en: A disrespectable conduct, acts opposed to those laid down in the scriptures, crookedness and cruelty, and abstention from sacrifices and other scriptural acts that lead to merit, show one's impurity of birth.

sa: यात्रामात्रं च भुञ्जीत केवलं प्राणयात्रिकम्। धर्मलब्धमथाश्नीयान्न काममनुवर्तयेत्॥
en: He should cat just enough for livelihood, the maintenance of life. He should eat only such food as has been got by fair means, and should not pursue the dictates of desire.

sa: कालिकाश्रममासाद्य विपाशायां कृतोदकः। ब्रह्मचारी जितक्रोधस्त्रिरात्रं मुच्यते भवात्॥
en: If a person, controlling his anger, and observing the vow of Brahmacharya for three days, bathes in the river Vipasa at the hermitage called Kalika, he is sure to get over rebirth.

sa: जघान तारकं चापि दैत्यमन्यांस्तथासुरान्। त्रिदशेन्द्राज्ञया ब्राँल्लोकानां हितकाम्यया॥
en: He killed the Daitya Taraka as also many other Asuras, at the command of the king of the celestials, O Brahmana, and moved also by the desire of benefiting all the worlds.

sa: विवृद्धमूषिका रथ्या विभिन्नमणिकास्तथा। केशा नखाश्च सुप्तानामद्यन्ते मूषिकैर्निशि॥
en: The streets swarmed with rats and mice. Earthen pots showed cracks or broken from no visible cause. At night, the rats and mice ate away the hair and nails of sleeping men.

sa: ओषधीयम्सम्पन्ना नगान् पुष्पफलान्वितान्। काननोपलशैलांश्च ददाति वसुधां ददत्॥
en: The man who makes a gift of earth is considered as giving away herbs and plants possessed of high and efficacious virtues, trees adorned with flowers and fruit, charming forests, and hillocks.

sa: बलिकर्मसु वक्ष्यामि गुणान् कर्मफलोदयान्। देवयक्षोरगनृणां भूतानामथ रक्षसाम्॥
en: I shall now describe to you the merits, with the fruits they bring about, of Bali offerings man own made to the celestials, the Yakshas, the Uragas, human beings, spirits and Rakshasas.
